stem_text: A wind-powered generator converts wind energy into electrical energy. Assume that the generator converts a fixed fraction of the wind energy intercepted by its blades into electrical energy. For wind speed 𝑣 , the electrical power output will be most likely proportional to

candidate_solve.derivation: Mass of air intercepted per second: dm/dt = rho * A * v. Kinetic energy per unit time of this intercepted air: P_wind = (1/2)*(dm/dt)*v^2 = (1/2)*rho*A*v^3. Since electrical power output is a fixed fraction of wind power, P_elec proportional to v^3.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Mass flow rate scaling dm/dt proportional to v, kinetic energy proportional to v^2

representation_translation.evidence: Combining mass flux and kinetic energy into power rate equation

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Single proportionality chain dm/dt ~ v => P ~ (dm/dt)*v^2 ~ v^3

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Avoiding quadratic distractor v^2 (which assumes constant mass rather than fluid flux)

demand_proposal.rationale: Applying mass-flux kinetic energy scaling to windmill power generation
